metadata.title: Christmas Holiday Treats : How to Make Eggnog
metadata.description:
Nothing spices up a holiday gathering like homemade spiked eggnog, and this recipe incorporates bourbon, brandy, whipped cream, cinnamon and nutmeg. Prepare this holiday favorite for your guests with help from a professional chef in this free video on Christmas sweets.

Expert: Michelle Karam
Contact: www.DishesByMichelle.com
Bio: Michelle Karam is a mom, a professional chef and a TV culinary host.
Filmmaker: Geffner Productions

Series Description: The holiday season is a time for gathering friends and family around a bountiful table. Prepare these heartfelt holiday recipes with demonstrations from a professional chef in this free video series on Christmas feast recipes.

summary.brief: Chef Michelle Karam prepares a festive spiked eggnog.
summary.detailed: The video opens with Michelle Karam, wearing a green short‑sleeve top, at a kitchen island decorated with nutcrackers and a red placemat. She cracks six eggs, separates the yolks into a decorative bowl and reserves the whites. One cup of sugar is added to the yolks and she beats the mixture for about ten minutes until it turns thick and buttery yellow. She slowly pours one cup of bourbon and 3/8 cup of brandy into the bowl while continuing to mix for several more minutes. The bowl is covered and placed in the refrigerator for a few hours. After chilling, she stirs in three cups of whole milk and ¾ teaspoon of ground nutmeg. In separate bowls she whips heavy cream to stiff peaks and also whips the reserved egg whites to stiff peaks. She gently folds the whipped cream into the chilled yolk‑milk mixture, then folds in the whipped egg whites, preserving the airy texture. The finished eggnog is poured into clear glasses, a pinch of nutmeg is sprinkled on top, and she takes a sip while smiling.

action.detailed: Beat the yolks with sugar, blend in bourbon and brandy, chill, add milk and nutmeg, whip cream and egg whites to stiff peaks, fold both into the chilled mixture, pour into glasses, garnish with nutmeg, and taste.
action.actor: Chef Michelle Karam, the woman in the green top

summary.brief: Chef Michelle Karam makes a fluffy holiday eggnog by separating eggs, beating yolks with sugar, adding bourbon and brandy, then folding in milk, nutmeg, whipped cream and beaten egg‑white peaks.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with Michelle Karam introducing the holiday eggnog recipe. She cracks six eggs, separates the yolks from the whites and reserves the whites for later. She adds one cup of sugar to the yolks and beats the mixture for several minutes until it becomes thick, pale‑butter colored and stiff. She slowly pours in one cup of bourbon and 3/8 cup of brandy, mixing continuously for a few more minutes until fully incorporated, then covers the bowl and chills it in the refrigerator. After chilling, she removes the mixture, adds three cups of whole milk and 3/4 teaspoon of nutmeg, whisking to combine and breaking up any clumps. In separate bowls she whips heavy cream to stiff peaks and beats the reserved egg whites to stiff peaks. She gently folds both the whipped cream and the beaten egg whites into the chilled yolk‑milk mixture, turning from the center outward so the airy texture is preserved. The finished eggnog has a light beige, buttery color and a fluffy consistency; she notes it can be chilled again or served immediately.

Nothing spices up a holiday gathering like homemade spiked eggnog, and this recipe incorporates bourbon, brandy, whipped cream, cinnamon and nutmeg. Prepare this holiday favorite for your guests with help from a professional chef in this free video on Christmas sweets.

Contact: www.DishesByMichelle.com
Bio: Michelle Karam is a mom, a professional chef and a TV culinary host.

summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with Michelle Karam, wearing a green short‑sleeve top, at a kitchen island decorated with nutcrackers and a red placemat. She cracks six eggs, separates the yolks into a decorative bowl and reserves the whites. One cup of sugar is added to the yolks and she beats the mixture for about ten minutes until it turns thick and buttery yellow. She slowly pours one cup of bourbon and 3/8 cup of brandy into the bowl while continuing to mix for several more minutes. The bowl is covered and placed in the refrigerator for a few hours. After chilling, she stirs in three cups of whole milk and ¾ teaspoon of ground nutmeg. In separate bowls she whips heavy cream to stiff peaks and also whips the reserved egg whites to stiff peaks. She gently folds the whipped cream into the chilled yolk‑milk mixture, then folds in the whipped egg whites, preserving the airy texture. The finished eggnog is poured into clear glasses, a pinch of nutmeg is sprinkled on top, and she takes a sip while smiling.
